items.q: Why begin mental health work from strength instead of pathology?
items.a: Conti's frame: there's **far more going right than wrong** if you're alive and seeking growth. **"What's going right"** is truth-aligned, not toxic positivity — it lets you change from **power, not helplessness**.

items.q: What is the only crucial ingredient for self-inquiry?
items.a: **Compassionate curiosity** — light-hearted or serious exploration without fear of what you'll find. Fear and stigma make aloneness unnecessarily anxiety-provoking.

items.q: Should you only act, or only introspect?
items.a: Neither extreme. Map your **doing-vs-thinking profile**. Too much doing → diminishing returns; too little → **learned helplessness**. Low reflection can work if generative drive is on and life is going well.

items.q: Why externalize thoughts instead of only ruminating?
items.a: **Speech and writing** activate different error-checking than internal loops. External tests help you avoid **self-referential bigotry** — quiet vs hyperverbal is not the same as organized vs anxious.

items.q: What does an examined-life laundry list usually reveal?
items.a: Ask: how much are you **choosing** vs running on reflex? Intensive work often finds only ~**10–20%** of reported life is truly valued — the rest is **accumulated momentum** (~80% autopilot).

items.q: What does "X marks the spot" mean in Conti's method?
items.a: **Draining patterns** (e.g. repeating dead-end dates while wanting a partner) show where to dig. Change via **collaborative small wins** — one gym visit beats five failed attempts.

items.q: Why isn't doing the opposite of your parents enough?
items.a: Replicating a childhood pattern **or** overcorrecting both fail without understanding. **Insight** — not mere opposition — puts you in the **driver's seat**.

items.q: How does the anti-control instinct become an agency lever?
items.a: Humans **resist being controlled**. Realizing **you stand in your own way** (fear of failure, unworthiness, overcommitment) — not an enemy-self — defuses tension so you get **on the same page with yourself**.

items.q: What should you do with intrusive thoughts?
items.a: Audit **self-talk first** — loops can run **hundreds of times/day** and always carry meaning. Redirect after you understand the root; trauma's limbic system ignores the clock so "then" feels like "now."

items.q: How do you prime the unconscious toward a better bias?
items.a: Build a **positive climate**: photo walls of real memories (Larry Squire anecdote), "what went right" reviews — implicit registration that counters a default **negative self-talk climate**.

items.q: Is happy-go-lucky the goal of mental health?
items.a: No. Real happiness is **peace + contentment + capacity for delight**, holding tragedy awareness. Happy-go-lucky **avoids grounding**; an examined life is required for intentional living.
